transitions.p: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. ______ they are excellent swimmers, using their wings like flippers to move through the water.
transitions.e: The text contrasts what penguins can’t do with what they do well, so a contrast word fits.

transitions.p: The school’s solar panels produce more electricity than the building uses. ______ the extra power is sold back to the local utility.
transitions.e: Producing extra electricity leads to selling it, a cause and effect.

transitions.p: Many everyday foods come from plants in the grass family. ______ wheat, rice, and corn are all grasses.
transitions.e: The second sentence gives specific examples of the first.

transitions.p: To plant a tree, first dig a hole twice as wide as the root ball. ______ set the tree in the hole and fill it with soil.
transitions.e: The steps follow an order, so a sequence word fits.

transitions.p: Reading aloud helps young children learn new words. ______ it gives parents and children a chance to spend time together.
transitions.e: The second sentence adds another benefit.

transitions.p: The first attempt to climb the peak failed because of bad weather. ______ the team tried again the following year and reached the summit.
transitions.e: Despite the failure, they tried again, so a contrast word fits.

transitions.p: Most stars in the night sky appear to stay in fixed positions relative to one another. The planets, ______ shift their positions from week to week, which is why ancient astronomers called them “wanderers.”
transitions.e: Planets moving is set against stars staying fixed, so a contrast is needed.

transitions.p: Ice cream sales and sunburns both rise during the summer, but one doesn’t cause the other. Both are driven by a third factor: hot, sunny weather. ______ a correlation between two events doesn’t show that one produces the other.
transitions.e: The last sentence restates the point of the example in general terms.

transitions.p: Architect Julia Morgan designed more than seven hundred buildings during her career, including Hearst Castle. ______ she was the first woman admitted to the architecture program at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris.
transitions.e: The text adds another accomplishment, so an additive word fits.

transitions.p: Early telephones required an operator to connect each call by hand. As the number of subscribers grew, this system became slow and costly. ______ engineers developed automatic switching equipment that could route calls without human help.
transitions.e: The growing costs led to the new equipment, a cause and effect.

transitions.p: Some scientists describe the human gut as an ecosystem. ______ an ecosystem such as a forest, it contains many interacting species, and removing one can affect the others.
transitions.e: The sentence names a similarity between the gut and a forest.

transitions.p: Critics expected the small film to disappear from theaters within a week. ______ it ran for six months and earned twenty times its budget.
transitions.e: What happened replaced what was expected, so “Instead” fits.

transitions.p: Economists often assume that people respond to incentives in predictable ways. Paying blood donors, it would seem, should increase donations. ______ in some studies, offering small payments actually reduced donations, apparently because payment turned an act of generosity into a mere transaction.
transitions.e: The result runs against the expected outcome. “Accordingly” and “Likewise” imply the result fits the expectation.

transitions.p: The sculptor Barbara Hepworth rejected the idea that her abstract forms were removed from nature. Her pierced stone shapes, she insisted, grew from the hills and coast of Cornwall. ______ although her work contains no literal landscapes, she considered it deeply rooted in place.
transitions.e: The final sentence draws a conclusion from her statements. “Nevertheless” would wrongly signal a contradiction; the “although” already handles the contrast within the sentence.

transitions.p: Glass appears to be a solid, and in everyday life it behaves like one. At the atomic level, ______ its structure lacks the orderly repeating pattern of a crystal, resembling instead a liquid frozen in place.
transitions.e: The atomic structure differs from the everyday appearance, so a contrast is needed.

transitions.p: In 1854, physician John Snow mapped cholera deaths in London and traced them to a single water pump. Most of his colleagues believed the disease spread through foul air. Snow’s map, ______ did more than stop one outbreak: it challenged the prevailing theory of how disease travels.
transitions.e: “Then” here means “therefore”: it sums up the significance of the facts given. The others would signal a simultaneous event or a contrast that isn’t there.

transitions.p: Some historians argue that the invention of the mechanical clock transformed medieval labor by making time something that could be measured and sold. ______ others caution that for centuries most rural workers continued to organize their days by the sun and the seasons, so the change was slower than this account implies.
transitions.e: The second group of historians qualifies the first group’s claim, so a contrast is needed. “Indeed” would support it.

transitions.p: Astronomers had predicted that the comet would break apart on its close pass by the Sun. Observers watched as its bright tail faded and vanished behind the solar disk. ______ hours later, a smaller but intact comet emerged on the other side, to the astonishment of researchers.
transitions.e: The events follow in time, and the emergence wasn’t caused by the fading. “Therefore” would wrongly claim a logical result.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to state when the bridge opened. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Golden Gate Bridge connects San Francisco and Marin County.
• Construction began in 1933.
• The bridge opened in 1937.
• It is painted a color called International Orange.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: The Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937.
w: Construction on the Golden Gate Bridge began in 1933.
The Golden Gate Bridge connects San Francisco and Marin County.
The Golden Gate Bridge is painted International Orange.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice gives the opening date.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to explain why the plant is called a sunflower. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sunflowers can grow more than ten feet tall.
• Young sunflowers turn to face the sun as it moves across the sky.
• Their seeds are used to make oil.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Sunflowers get their name because young plants turn to face the sun.
w: Sunflowers can grow more than ten feet tall.
Sunflower seeds are used to make oil.
Sunflowers are tall plants with useful seeds.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: The goal is the reason for the name, which is the turning behavior.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to compare the sizes of the two animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• African elephants can weigh up to 14,000 pounds.
• Asian elephants can weigh up to 11,000 pounds.
• African elephants have larger ears.
• Both species live in herds.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: African elephants can weigh up to 14,000 pounds, while Asian elephants reach about 11,000 pounds.
w: Both African and Asian elephants live in herds.
African elephants have larger ears and live in herds.
Asian elephants can weigh up to 11,000 pounds.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice gives both animals’ sizes.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to introduce the author to readers unfamiliar with her. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Octavia Butler was an American science fiction writer.
• She published Kindred in 1979.
• She won two Hugo Awards.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Octavia Butler, an American science fiction writer, won two Hugo Awards.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: An introduction should say who she is. Only this choice identifies her.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to emphasize how long the trail is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Appalachian Trail runs through fourteen states.
• It is about 2,190 miles long.
• It was completed in 1937.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: At about 2,190 miles, the Appalachian Trail stretches through fourteen states.
w: The Appalachian Trail was completed in 1937.
Hikers can visit the Appalachian Trail.
The Appalachian Trail is an American trail that was completed long ago.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: This choice uses the mileage and number of states to show its length.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to present the main use of the invention. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Stephanie Kwolek was a chemist at DuPont.
• In 1965, she invented Kevlar.
• Kevlar is a strong, lightweight fiber.
• It is mainly used in protective vests.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Kevlar, invented by Stephanie Kwolek, is mainly used in protective vests.
w: Stephanie Kwolek was a chemist at DuPont.
Kevlar is a fiber that is strong and lightweight.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice states the use.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Two 2019 studies examined how urban noise affects birds.
• One study, in Madrid, tracked great tits for three years.
• The other, in Toronto, tracked song sparrows for one breeding season.
• Both found that birds near loud roads sang at higher pitches.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: While the Madrid study tracked great tits for three years, the Toronto study followed song sparrows for just one breeding season.
w: Both 2019 studies found that birds near loud roads sang at higher pitches.
Two 2019 studies, one in Madrid and one in Toronto, examined how urban noise affects birds.
Great tits and song sparrows both sang at higher pitches near loud roads.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: The goal is a difference, which is the species and duration. The others state what the studies share.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to explain the significance of the discovery. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Rosetta Stone was found in Egypt in 1799.
• It bears the same text in three scripts: hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Ancient Greek.
• Scholars could already read Ancient Greek.
• Using the Greek, Jean-François Champollion deciphered hieroglyphs in 1822.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Because the Rosetta Stone repeated one text in three scripts, including readable Greek, it enabled scholars to decipher hieroglyphs.
w: The Rosetta Stone, found in Egypt in 1799, bears text in three scripts.
Jean-François Champollion deciphered hieroglyphs in 1822, and the stone was found in 1799.
Hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Ancient Greek are the three scripts on the Rosetta Stone.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Significance means why it mattered: it unlocked hieroglyphs. The others only report facts.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to present the study’s finding to an audience unfamiliar with tardigrades. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tardigrades are microscopic animals found in moss and water.
• In 2007, researchers exposed tardigrades to the vacuum of space.
• Many of them survived and later reproduced.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Tardigrades, microscopic animals found in moss and water, survived exposure to the vacuum of space in a 2007 study.
w: In 2007, researchers conducted a study in space.
Many tardigrades survived and later reproduced.
Tardigrades can be found in moss and in water.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: The audience needs to know what tardigrades are plus the finding. Only this choice has both.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to emphasize the artist’s achievement in spite of obstacles. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Edmonia Lewis was a sculptor born in 1844.
• She was of African American and Ojibwe descent.
• She faced racial discrimination in the United States.
• She moved to Rome and won international fame.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Despite facing racial discrimination in the United States, Edmonia Lewis won international fame as a sculptor.
w: Edmonia Lewis, who was born in 1844, was of African American and Ojibwe descent.
Edmonia Lewis was a sculptor who moved from the United States to Rome.
Rome was the city where the sculptor Edmonia Lewis lived.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: “Despite” links the obstacle to her achievement. The others omit one or both.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to explain how the technique works. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Crop rotation is the practice of changing what is grown in a field each year.
• Beans add nitrogen to soil.
• Corn uses large amounts of nitrogen.
• Farmers have used crop rotation for centuries.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: In crop rotation, a farmer might follow beans, which add nitrogen to soil, with corn, which uses a lot of it.
w: Farmers have used crop rotation for centuries.
Corn uses large amounts of nitrogen from the soil.
Beans and corn are two crops that farmers have grown for centuries.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Explaining how it works requires connecting the two crops’ effects on nitrogen.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to describe the purpose of the program. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Svalbard Global Seed Vault opened in Norway in 2008.
• It stores duplicates of seeds from gene banks around the world.
• It is built into a mountain above the Arctic Circle.
• Its aim is to safeguard crop diversity against disasters.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault stores duplicate seeds to safeguard crop diversity against disasters.
w: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, opened in 2008, is located in Norway.
Built into a mountain, the Svalbard Global Seed Vault lies above the Arctic Circle.
Gene banks around the world contribute seeds to a vault in a mountain.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice states what the vault is for.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to emphasize that the two scholars reached a similar conclusion by different methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Historian Lena Brandt studied shipping records from a medieval port.
• She concluded that the port’s decline began around 1340.
• Archaeologist Tomás Rey excavated warehouses at the same port.
• Pottery layers led him to date the decline to the mid-1300s.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Working from shipping records and from excavated pottery, respectively, Brandt and Rey each dated the port’s decline to the mid-fourteenth century.
w: Brandt, a historian, and Rey, an archaeologist, both studied a medieval port that declined.
Rey excavated warehouses and pottery layers, while Brandt read shipping records from the port.
Although Brandt dated the decline to around 1340, Rey found evidence for a different period.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice names both methods and the shared result. The last wrong choice invents a disagreement.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to acknowledge a limitation of the study while presenting its main result. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2021 study tested a reading program in twelve rural schools.
• Students in the program improved their reading scores by 15 percent.
• Scores of similar students outside the program rose 6 percent.
• The study didn’t include any urban schools.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Students in the reading program outpaced their peers, gaining 15 percent versus 6 percent, though the study included only rural schools.
w: A 2021 study tested a reading program in twelve rural schools and did not include urban schools.
Students in the reading program improved their scores by 15 percent, more than the 6 percent improvement of similar students.
Because the study did not include urban schools, the 15 percent improvement among rural students cannot be measured.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: This choice gives both the result and the limitation. The last choice falsely says the improvement can’t be measured.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to present the theory as a challenge to an earlier view. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• For much of the twentieth century, geologists held that continents were fixed in place.
• In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed that continents slowly drift.
• He cited matching fossils on separate continents.
• His idea gained acceptance after seafloor spreading was discovered in the 1960s.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Wegener’s 1912 proposal that continents drift, supported by matching fossils, contradicted the view that continents were fixed in place.
w: Alfred Wegener cited matching fossils on separate continents when he proposed his idea in 1912.
Seafloor spreading, discovered in the 1960s, led to the acceptance of Wegener’s idea.
Geologists in the twentieth century studied continents, fossils, and the seafloor.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice sets his theory against the earlier view.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to use the example to support the claim that public art can change how a neighborhood is perceived. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2005, artists in Philadelphia began painting murals on buildings in a run-down district.
• More than 200 murals were completed by 2015.
• Surveys found that the share of visitors describing the district as “welcoming” rose from 22 percent to 61 percent.
• Property taxes in the district stayed about the same.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: After more than 200 murals appeared in a Philadelphia district, the share of visitors calling it “welcoming” rose from 22 percent to 61 percent.
w: Between 2005 and 2015, artists completed more than 200 murals in a Philadelphia district.
Property taxes in a Philadelphia district stayed about the same after artists painted murals there.
Artists in Philadelphia began painting murals in a run-down district in 2005.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Perception is measured by the survey, so this choice links the murals to the change. The others report activity or taxes.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to highlight what is unusual about the species’ reproduction compared with that of most fish. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Most fish species leave their eggs unattended.
• Seahorses live in shallow coastal waters.
• In seahorses, the female deposits eggs in a pouch on the male.
• The male carries the eggs until they hatch.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Whereas most fish leave their eggs unattended, male seahorses carry eggs in a pouch until they hatch.
w: Seahorses, which live in shallow coastal waters, are a kind of fish that reproduces.
The female seahorse deposits her eggs in a pouch on the male.
Most fish species leave their eggs unattended, and many live in the ocean.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: The goal requires a comparison with most fish and the unusual trait. The second choice gives only the trait, without the comparison.

rhetorical_synthesis.s: The student wants to explain why the policy’s results surprised its designers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
rhetorical_synthesis.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A city offered rebates to households that bought efficient appliances.
• Planners expected electricity use to fall by 10 percent.
• Electricity use fell by only 2 percent.
• Follow-up surveys found that many households kept their old appliances running as well, in garages and basements.
rhetorical_synthesis.r: Planners expected a 10 percent drop in electricity use, but because many households kept running their old appliances alongside the new ones, use fell only 2 percent.
w: A city’s rebates led households to buy efficient appliances, and electricity use fell by 2 percent.
Follow-up surveys found that many households kept old appliances in garages and basements.
Planners expected electricity use to fall by 10 percent after offering rebates for efficient appliances.
rhetorical_synthesis.e: Only this choice contrasts the expectation with the result and gives the reason.
